# QS-CFW-9497-56 - Quality specification - flange blank CFW-9497-56 (4140) Rev A

Scope
- This quality specification applies to raw forged flange blanks identified as CFW-9497-56 produced at Plant P1. It defines acceptance criteria, inspection methods, and nonconformance handling for material, dimensional tolerance, hardness, and weight control for the stated part.
- The document covers incoming material verification from the heat treatment supplier, production forging release inspection at P1, and final inspection prior to delivery to the machining cell. It does not supersede customer drawing notes; where customer drawing and this specification conflict, escalate to engineering for disposition.

Requirements table
- Part: CFW-9497-56
- Material: 4140 (as specified on purchase order)
- Hardness: The hardness range for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 31-34 HRC.
- Bore diameter tolerance: The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is ±0.03 mm.
- Maximum forging weight: The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 57.2 kg.
- Surface condition: Forged surfaces shall be free from scale, laps, cracks, and other discontinuities that would prevent machining or cause rejection under visual acceptance criteria.
- Identification: Each blank shall be identified with batch and heat information legibly marked or tagged to support traceability to mill test reports and heat treatment records.

Inspection method
Background and rationale
- Inspection steps prioritize traceability and prevention of downstream rejection. Hardness is verified on the forging as received to confirm heat treatment stability prior to machining. Bore dimensional control is critical for assembly fit; therefore, inspection uses calibrated gauges and measurement procedures that target the bore specified on the drawing. Weight control ensures die wear or fill issues are identified early; a maximum forging weight limit is specified to prevent overfilled impressions that could hide defects or exceed handling constraints.

Measurement procedures
- Hardness verification: Select at least two locations on each blank representative of the region specified on the drawing. Perform hardness testing using a calibrated portable hardness tester following the manufacturer procedure and accepted method in the plant quality manual. Record each reading and the location on the part. If readings fall within the specified range, mark the part as inspected. If any reading is outside the specified range, follow nonconformance handling.
- Bore measurement: Measure the bore using calibrated bore gauges or coordinate measurement equipment set up to measure the feature specified on the customer drawing. The bore will be accepted only if measured values fall within the nominal dimension plus or minus the specified tolerance. The bore diameter tolerance for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is ±0.03 mm. Record measurement device identification, calibration status, operator, and measurement results in the inspection record.
- Weight verification: Weigh each blank on a calibrated scale and record the value. The maximum forging weight for flange blank CFW-9497-56 (CFW-9497-56) is 57.2 kg. If the measured weight exceeds that value, quarantine the part and initiate nonconformance handling.
- Visual and dimensional inspection: Conduct a visual inspection for surface defects and a dimensional check of key features as specified on the drawing. Use calibrated instruments for critical dimensions. Document the inspector, date, and inspection station.

Examples and acceptance rationale
- Example acceptance scenario: A blank with hardness readings of values within the stated hardness range, a bore measurement within the specified bore diameter tolerance, and a weight below the maximum forging weight is released to machining. The combination of checks ensures metallurgical properties and dimensional conformity prior to further processing.
- Example rejection scenario: A blank with a hardness reading below the lower limit of the specified hardness range or above the upper limit, or with a bore measurement falling outside the specified bore diameter tolerance, or with a measured weight above the maximum forging weight shall be treated as nonconforming.

Records to keep
- Maintain a traceable inspection record for each batch that includes:
  - Part identifier and batch or heat number.
  - Material certificate reference from the mill.
  - Hardness test locations, individual readings, device identification, and calibration status.
  - Bore measurement results, measurement device identification, calibration status, operator, and date.
  - Measured weight and scale identification and calibration status.
  - Visual inspection findings and disposition.
  - Inspector name or identifier and date of inspection.
- Store records in the plant document control system for retention according to Plant P1 retention policy and to support customer or internal audits.

Nonconformance handling
- Identification and segregation: Any blank that fails to meet any requirement in the requirements table shall be immediately identified as nonconforming, tagged, and moved to the nonconforming material area. Do not return nonconforming blanks to inventory or machining without formal disposition.
- Notification and documentation: The inspector shall complete a nonconformance report that describes the failed characteristic, reference to this specification, measured values, and any immediate containment actions. Include supporting records such as hardness printouts, bore measurement records, and weight records.
- Disposition options: Engineering or quality shall review the nonconformance report and determine disposition. Possible dispositions include rework, use-as-is with documented concession, return to supplier, or scrap. Rework must have a documented method and acceptance criteria and shall be approved by engineering before execution.
- Example disposition rationale: If a blank exceeds the maximum forging weight, engineering may determine that the excess indicates overfill and potential internal defects; return to supplier or scrap may be appropriate. If a hardness reading is marginal and consistent across the batch, engineering may require full batch testing or heat-treatment rework.
- Final verification: Any product released from nonconforming status must be re-inspected and documented. The re-inspection record shall reference the original nonconformance report and show evidence that the disposition criteria have been met.

Revision control
- This revision applies to flange blanks CFW-9497-56 produced at Plant P1 and is Rev A. All inspectors and engineers working with this part shall follow the procedures and recordkeeping detailed above.
